title: From Modified Newtonian Gravity to a Maxwell-Type Gravitational Interaction
content: This paper continues a classical-mechanical approach, in which a modified Newtonian gravitational model was previously developed within a four-dimensional geometrical framework.  In that construction, classical kinetic energy \(T = mv^2/2\) leads naturally to a Minkowski metric and an action-based formulation of the equations of motion.  The present paper extends this model by examining two distinct energetic regimes and the corresponding forms of gravitational forces.  In the subcritical regime \(T < mc^2/2\), the modified Newtonian force \(\mathbf{F}_{Ne}\) provides a retrograde contribution to the perihelion advance.  A complementary velocity-dependent gravitomagnetic interaction \(\mathbf{F}_{gm}\) is constructed from the angular-motion law \(r^2 e^{2\varrho/r} d_t \varphi = \text{const.}\) and the no-work condition \(\mathbf{F}_{gm} \cdot \mathbf{v} = 0\).  Together, these forces reproduce the observed perihelion advance.  The limiting energetic regime \(T = mv^2/2\) is treated separately by imposing the energy condition \(k - T = 0\) as an active constraint.  Its dynamical implementation is formulated within a reduced Lagrange--d'Alembert-type multiplier approach, in which the radial inertial reaction is determined by the compatibility of the reduced radial equation of motion with the differentiated energy constraint.  For a light ray, the resulting total gravitational force yields the deflection angle \(\Delta \theta = 4GM/(bc^2)\) in the first-order weak-field approximation.  Finally, the gravitational model provides a classical-mechanical interpretation of the Michelson--Morley null result, giving equal round-trip propagation times \(2h/c\), along the parallel and transverse arms.  The results extend the model without assuming the invariance of the speed of light as an independent postulate.
